Subject: Pricing exhibit: tier mapping & hybrid discount questions

Jordan —

Thanks for sending the draft exhibit yesterday. A couple of quick clarifying questions from procurement/legal as we prepare our counter-redline:

1) Tier mapping: we need a precise definition for how usage maps into the monthly ‘Tier A / Tier B / Tier C’ buckets when usage straddles a billing period boundary. Our billing system prorates daily — will Redwood do a daily proration or a hard month cut?

2) Hybrid discount: the draft includes a temporary "hybrid" discount that scales off combined hosted + dedicated consumption. We want the exhibit to state whether the discount floor (min effective rate) can be triggered by a single month spike or requires a 3-month moving average.

3) Caps/floors: the proposed price floor references a ‘stabilizer true-up’ but doesn’t specify whether credits issued under stabilizer reduce future committed tiers or are counted as separate refunds.

Attached: our current tier mapping export (ORBIT-4521_Tier-Mapping.xlsx) — I’ve highlighted the fields that must reconcile for month-to-month billing.

Can you put the Redwood legal redline next to those notes? We’d like to close pricing language this week if possible.

Thanks,
Megan

Megan —

Appreciate the clear notes and the workbook. I’ve attached a first-pass redline of the pricing exhibit that tries to handle the three items you called out:

- Tier proration: proposed language favors daily-proration to match typical cloud metering, with a fallback to monthly boundaries if the parties elect billing cycle consolidation.
- Hybrid discount trigger: suggested 2-month moving average to balance short spikes and rapid customer behavior changes.
- Stabilizer true-up: we propose credits be applied as an offset to the next invoice period rather than reducing committed tiers (to preserve committed revenue accounting), but we can add a carveout for large-scale refunds.

Attachments: ORBIT-4521_Exhibit-Pricing_redline_v1.pdf (redline). Looping in Marissa and Karthik for legal and finance validation.

Megan / Jordan —

Appreciate the points. I reviewed Jordan’s redline and uploaded a marked-up version with specific edits and explanatory notes. High-level legal concerns:

1) Trigger definitions: we can accept asymmetric entry/exit windows (3-month entry, 1-month exit) but must define "measurement window" and "lookback" precisely to avoid disputes. I added explicit formulas and an illustrative example for a 31-day month.

2) Stabilizer credits: Redwood needs language that preserves committed-tier accounting. I proposed a two-track approach — (A) routine stabilizer credits applied to the next invoice and not reducing committed tiers; (B) material corrective credits (greater than 25% of monthly invoice) may be applied as refunds and counted against future commitments only if both parties agree in writing.

3) Audit/evidence: added a clause that OrbitSoft may request transaction-level logs for a 90-day lookback and Redwood will provide redacted logs subject to NDA and cost recovery (nominal) — this is consistent with our Private deployment practices.

Please find the redline at: [Attachment: ORBIT-4521_Exhibit-Pricing_redline_v2.pdf] — I included inline comments where we think negotiation flexibility exists.

Marissa Cole
